chapters.title: The God of All Comfort
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 1

Greeting

1Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Timothy, to the church of God that is in Corinth, with all the saints throughout Achaia:

2grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

The God of All Comfort

3Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and God of all comfort,

4who comforts us in all our trouble, so that we can comfort those who are in any trouble with the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.

5For as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so through Christ our comfort overflows too.

6If we are troubled, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which works in you when you patiently endure the same sufferings that we suffer.

7Our hope for you is firm, for we know that as you share in our sufferings, so you also share in our comfort.

8We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the trouble we went through in Asia. We were so utterly weighed down, beyond our strength, that we despaired even of life.

9Indeed, we felt within ourselves that we had received the sentence of death, so that we would not rely on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.

10He rescued us from so deadly a peril, and He will rescue us; on Him we have set our hope that He will rescue us again,

11as you also help us by your prayers, so that many will give thanks on our behalf for the gift granted us through the prayers of many.

Yes in Christ

12For this is our boast, the testimony of our conscience: that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and above all toward you, with holiness and godly sincerity, not by earthly wisdom but by the grace of God.

13For we write you nothing other than what you read and understand, and I hope you will understand fully,

14as you have understood us in part, that we are your boast as you are ours on the day of our Lord Jesus.

15Sure of this, I wanted to come to you first, so that you might have a second grace.

16I meant to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and to come back to you from Macedonia and have you send me on my way to Judea.

17When I wanted to do this, did I make my plans lightly? Or do I make my plans by worldly standards, ready to say "Yes, yes" and "No, no" at once?

18As God is faithful, our word to you has not been "Yes" and "No."

19For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we preached among you, Silvanus and Timothy and I, was not "Yes" and "No," but in Him it has always been "Yes."

20For all the promises of God find their "Yes" in Him. That is why it is through Him that we say our "Amen" to God, for His glory.

21It is God who makes us firm with you in Christ, and who has anointed us;

22He has also sealed us and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a pledge.

23I call on God as witness against my soul that it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.

24Not that we lord it over your faith; we work with you for your joy, for you stand firm in your faith.

Notes

  • vv3–7 "the God of all comfort, who comforts us… so that we can comfort" — paraklēsis and parakaleō, comfort, ten times in five verses. It is Isaiah's word in the Greek, Comfort, comfort My people (Isaiah 40:1), and I, I am He who comforts you (51:12); and the word of the Advocate, paraklētos, whom Jesus promised (John 14:16). The comfort Paul receives is not for him to keep: it overflows to others as Christ's sufferings overflow to him.

  • vv19–20 "in Him it has always been 'Yes'… through Him that we say our 'Amen'" — Amen is a Hebrew word, from the root of being firm and sure (the trusted of Genesis 15:6). Isaiah calls the LORD Elohei amen, the God of truth, word for word the God of Amen (Isaiah 65:16). Every promise God made is Yes in Christ, and the church answers it with Amen.

  • vv21–22 "makes us firm… in Christ, and who has anointed us… sealed us and given us the Spirit… as a pledge" — Christon… chrisas: Christ means the Anointed, and God has anointed those who are in Him. Arrabōn, pledge, is a Hebrew word in Greek letters, the pledge Judah left with Tamar, Your seal and your cord, and your staff (Genesis 38:18), in the Greek arrabōn. The seal and the pledge there were the token that the full payment would come; here the Spirit is that token.

chapters.title: The Aroma of Christ
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 2

The Letter Written in Tears

1For I made up my mind not to come to you again in sorrow.

2If I cause you sorrow, who is there to make me glad but the one I have made sorrowful?

3I wrote as I did so that when I came I would not be made sorrowful by those who should have made me rejoice, for I am confident about all of you, that my joy is the joy of you all.

4For I wrote to you out of much trouble and anguish of heart and with many tears, not to cause you sorrow but to let you know the love I have, more than enough, for you.

Forgive Him

5If anyone has caused sorrow, he has caused it not to me but in some measure, not to overstate it, to all of you.

6The punishment given by the majority is enough for such a man,

7so that now you should rather forgive and comfort him, or he may be overwhelmed by too much sorrow.

8So I urge you to confirm your love for him.

9For this is why I wrote: to test you and see whether you are obedient in everything.

10Anyone you forgive, I forgive too. What I have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven for your sake in the presence of Christ,

11so that we would not be outwitted by Satan, for we are not unaware of his schemes.

Led in Triumph

12When I came to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ, though a door was opened for me in the Lord,

13my spirit had no rest because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.

14But thanks be to God, who in Christ always leads us in His triumphal procession, and through us spreads everywhere the aroma of the knowledge of Him.

15For we are the fragrance of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing,

16to the one an aroma from death to death, to the other an aroma from life to life. Who is sufficient for these things?

17For we are not like so many, peddling the word of God, but as men of sincerity, as from God, we speak before God in Christ.

Notes

  • v14 "who in Christ always leads us in His triumphal procession" — thriambeuonti, the word of a victor's march through the city with his captives behind him; Paul uses it once more, of God leading the rulers and authorities in triumph over them (Colossians 2:15). Whether Paul sees himself as a captive led in Christ's train or as a soldier sharing the victory, the verb does not say; either way the triumph is God's.

  • vv14–16 "the aroma of the knowledge of Him… the fragrance of Christ to God… an aroma from death to death… from life to life" — osmē, aroma, and euōdia, fragrance, are the two words of the Law's soothing aroma to the LORD, osmē euōdias in the Greek (Leviticus 1:9), the smoke of the offering rising to God. Paul splits the phrase between his three lines: the apostles themselves are the offering, and the same smell is life to some and death to others.

chapters.title: The Veil Removed
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 3

A Letter from Christ

1Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some do, letters of recommendation to you or from you?

2You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.

3You show that you are a letter from Christ, delivered by us, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of hearts of flesh.

4Such is the confidence we have through Christ toward God.

5Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to reckon anything as coming from us; our sufficiency is from God,

6who has made us sufficient to be ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

The Greater Glory

7Now if the ministry of death, carved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the sons of Israel could not look steadily at Moses' face because of its glory, a glory that was being done away with,

8will not the ministry of the Spirit have even more glory?

9For if there was glory in the ministry that brought condemnation, the ministry that brings righteousness overflows with far more glory.

10Indeed, what once had glory has no glory at all in this respect, because of the glory that surpasses it.

11For if what was being done away with came with glory, much more will what remains have glory.

The Veil

12Since we have such a hope, we are very bold,

13not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel might not look steadily at the end of what was being done away with.

14But their minds were hardened. For to this very day, when the old covenant is read, that same veil remains, not lifted, because only in Christ is it done away with.

15Yes, to this day whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their hearts.

16But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

17Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

18We all, with unveiled face, beholding the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another, as from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

Notes

  • v3 "not on tablets of stone but on tablets of hearts of flesh" — the two covenants side by side. The first was tablets of stone, written by the finger of God (Exodus 31:18); the new is the promise of Ezekiel, I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh (Ezekiel 36:26), and of Jeremiah, on their heart I will write it (Jeremiah 31:33).

  • vv7, 13 "the glory of his face… a veil over his face" — Exodus 34:29–35 in the Greek, where the skin of his face was glorified, dedoxastai. The Hebrew says the skin of his face had grown horns, qaran (see the note there), and the Greek is the reading Paul builds on. Exodus says Moses veiled his face after speaking to the people; it does not say the glory faded. That is Paul's reading, set against the glory that remains (v11).

  • vv14–17 "when the old covenant is read… whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away. Now the Lord is the Spirit" — tēs palaias diathēkēs, the old covenant, a phrase found only here in the New Testament. V16 is Exodus 34:34 in the Greek, When Moses went in before the LORD… he would take the veil off, with Moses went in changed to anyone turns. The Lord of that verse is YHWH, and Paul says who He is now met as: the Lord is the Spirit.

  • v18 "beholding the glory of the Lord as in a mirror" — katoptrizomenoi, in the New Testament only here, from katoptron, mirror. It can mean beholding as in a mirror, as Paul's we see in a mirror (1 Corinthians 13:12), or reflecting, as Moses' face shone back what it had seen. Metamorphoumetha, are being transformed, is the verb of Jesus transfigured (Mark 9:2) and of Romans 12:2.

chapters.title: Treasure in Clay Pots
chapters.html:
2 Corinthians 4

Light Out of Darkness

1Therefore, since we have this ministry by the mercy of God, we do not lose heart.

2We have renounced the shameful things that are done in secret. We do not use cunning or distort the word of God, but by openly stating the truth we commend ourselves to everyone's conscience in the sight of God.

3Even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.

4In their case the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelievers, so that they do not see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.

5For what we proclaim is not ourselves but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your slaves for Jesus' sake.

6For God, who said, "Light will shine out of darkness," is the one who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

Treasure in Clay Pots

7But we have this treasure in clay pots, to show that the surpassing power belongs to God and not to us.

8We are troubled on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;

9persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed;

10always carrying in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be shown in our bodies.

11For we who are alive are always being handed over to death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be shown in our mortal flesh.

12So death is at work in us, but life in you.

13Since we have the same Spirit of faith that is in what is written, "I believed, therefore I spoke," we also believe, and therefore we speak,

14knowing that He who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also with Jesus and bring us with you into His presence.

15All this is for your sake, so that as grace reaches more and more people, it may increase thanksgiving, to the glory of God.

The Eternal Weight of Glory

16So we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day.

17For this light and momentary trouble is producing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all comparison,

18as we look not to what is seen but to what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.

Notes

  • vv4, 6 "Christ, who is the image of God… God, who said, 'Light will shine out of darkness'… in the face of Jesus Christ" — the first day of creation, "Light — be." And light was (Genesis 1:3), joined to Isaiah's The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light (Isaiah 9:2), whose Greek has the same verb, light will shine on you. The God who made light at the beginning has made it shine again in the heart. The image of God is the word of humankind's making (Genesis 1:27), and the face is the answer to the veiled face of Moses (3:13): the glory once hidden is seen in Christ's face.

  • v13 "I believed, therefore I spoke" — Psalm 116:10 in the Greek. The Hebrew reads I believed, even when I said, "I am greatly afflicted": the psalmist kept faith in his suffering. Paul, troubled on every side (v8), takes up the same words.

  • v17 "an eternal weight of glory" — in Hebrew, kavod, glory, is from kaved, heavy, the word of Moses' heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue (Exodus 4:10). Paul sets the light, elaphron, trouble of now against glory that has weight.
